text:
The largest regular tetrahedron that can be cut from a $7\times7$ square using a parallelogram‑shaped net has side length $s = \frac{14}{3}$, giving a surface area  

\[
\text{Area}=4\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^{2}= \sqrt3\;s^{2}= \sqrt3\left(\frac{14}{3}\right)^{2}= \frac{196\sqrt3}{9}.
\]

ANSWER: \(\displaystyle \frac{196\sqrt3}{9}\)
